title: Meta Launches Standalone Seller App for Facebook Marketplace and Free Verification Badge
excerpt: The new app brings AI-powered listing tools to frequent sellers, while a selfie-based verification system aims to curb fraud on the platform's 1.1 billion-user marketplace.
body:
• Meta launched "Seller," a standalone iPhone app for frequent Facebook Marketplace sellers with AI-powered listing tools
  • Facebook Verified, a free selfie-based badge, confirms real people behind profiles — separate from the paid Meta Verified subscription
  • Marketplace handles 430 million monthly listings globally, with one in three young U.S. Facebook users visiting daily
  • The moves are part of Meta's strategy to build purpose-built apps for its most engaged user communities

Meta on Friday launched two significant additions to its Facebook ecosystem: a standalone Seller app for frequent Marketplace users and a free identity verification badge designed to signal that a real person is behind a profile.

The announcements come as the company pushes to strengthen Facebook Marketplace against e-commerce rivals like eBay while addressing persistent concerns about scams and fake accounts on the platform.

A Dedicated App for Sellers

The Seller app, now available on Apple's App Store for U.S. users 18 and older, is designed for people who regularly list items on Marketplace. It syncs with existing Marketplace accounts, carrying over current listings, messages, and sales history, according to Reuters.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=LdTuuOQ7poY

The app includes AI-powered tools that let sellers upload photos and receive automatically generated listings with suggested titles, descriptions, categories, and prices. It also offers a bulk listing feature, a unified inbox for buyer communications, inventory management, and performance data on views, clicks, and sold items, according to Gizmodo.

Meta is also testing an Android version and a web experience for those who download the app.

"I think about these as things that complement the main app, and cater to the more high-intensity user communities. That's the idea that underpins a lot of what we're doing this year."

— Tom Alison, Head of Facebook

Marketplace remains one of Facebook's most heavily used features. Globally, users post about 430 million items and 44 million vehicles each month. In the U.S., one in three young adults who use Facebook visits Marketplace daily, according to Meta.

Free Verification to Fight Fraud

Alongside the Seller app, Meta introduced Facebook Verified — a free badge that uses selfie-based facial recognition to confirm there is a real person behind a profile. Users record a short video selfie, which Meta checks against existing profile photos to verify a match, according to Fast Company.

Once verified, the badge appears across Marketplace, Dating, Groups, and the user's profile, with plans to extend it to Feed posts over time. The process is free and requires only a one-time verification.

The free badge is distinct from Meta Verified, the company's existing paid subscription that bundles verification with premium features like impersonation protection and direct account support. Paid plans range from $14.99 to $499.99 per month.

The verification push comes as Facebook remains a major starting point for fraud. Consumers reported losing more money in 2025 to scams originating on Facebook than on any other social media platform, according to the Federal Trade Commission. Across social media, reported losses reached $2.1 billion, with shopping scams the most frequently reported category.

Meta's Purpose-Built App Strategy

Seller is the second standalone app Meta has spun off from Facebook this year. In May, the company launched Forum, a dedicated app for Facebook Groups. Tom Alison, who heads Facebook, told The New York Times that the strategy is "very early" and "experimental," aimed at serving the most engaged segments of Facebook's massive user base.

Meta also announced a new full-screen video experience for Facebook, continuing its push to compete with TikTok and YouTube Shorts in short-form video.

What to Watch

For small business owners and side hustlers — including Indian diaspora entrepreneurs who use Marketplace to sell within their communities — the Seller app could simplify what has been a clunky process of managing listings within the main Facebook app. The AI listing tools, in particular, lower the barrier for sellers who list inventory frequently.

The free verification badge, meanwhile, could help legitimate sellers stand out in a marketplace where trust remains a persistent challenge. Whether it will meaningfully dent the platform's fraud problem remains to be seen.
nri_angle: Indian entrepreneurs and small business owners using Facebook Marketplace can benefit from dedicated selling tools and AI-powered listings to reach buyers in their communities.
author: Diaspora Desk
